Elisa: experimenting with continuous-batcher -> observed spikes when kernel sampler switches mid-batch. p95 jumps from ~180ms to ~1.1s for some requests. attaching tiny trace excerpt and perf notes. anyone seen kernel-flip-induced tails like this? cc @Mike H @Dan R

Mike H: yeah saw similar behavior. sampler flips + batch assembly mismatch causes extra memcpy and kernel recompile path on some older nodes. can you paste the short trace?

Elisa: pasted trace below:
```
[batch=4832] assemble_time=12ms kernel=wave seq_len=64 tokens=48
[batch=4832] kernel_switch -> wavkernel latency=420ms (first token)
[req=3347] wait_q=18ms batch_wait=6ms exec=112ms -> tail spike after switch ~1.2s
[batch=4833] assemble_time=9ms kernel=wavkernel seq_len=32 tokens=12
```

Dan R: quick thoughts: 1) increase token_budget_target for interactive lane 64->96 to reduce frequent kernel flips. 2) add a small hysteresis on sampler: require 2 consecutive sampling signals before swapping kernels. 3) min_batch_hold_ms=8 to let microbatches form slightly larger.

Sara K: we tried hysteresis before and saw throughput drop on conv-heavy workloads. might be ok if we pair with a probabilistic soft-429 policy: when a kernel change is detected, soft-reject 5-10% of new admits for 50ms so we can drain and re-form more homogeneous batches. reduces spikes but trades small request defers.

Elisa: rough config I'm thinking to canary (pseudo-yaml):
```
admission:
  lanes:
    interactive:
      token_budget_target: 96
      min_batch_hold_ms: 8
  sampler:
    hysteresis_count: 2
    kernel_stability_window_ms: 200
  soft_429:
    on_kernel_change:
      probability: 0.06
      hold_ms: 50
```

Mike H: sounds reasonable. let's canary on one podpool behind the canary selector. perf-bot can schedule the run. also profile GPU memcpy and nvml on that pool.

perf-bot: scheduled canary run on pool:runtime-canary-3. link: https://perf.redwood/canary/4129001234 (results will post when done)

Dan R: action items:
- profile memcpy & kernel transition paths on canary GPUs
- run canary with token_budget=96 + min_hold=8 + sampler.hysteresis=2
- measure p50/p95/p99 and soft-429 rate (target <1%)
- check kv-cache hit distribution before/after (kv hits reduce need for switching kernels) :mag:

Elisa: I'll kick it off this afternoon and post initial numbers here.

Sara K: if soft-429 rises, add alert: latency_p95>500ms && soft429_rate>1% -> rollback. also add dashboard metric for kernel_change_rate per minute.

Mike H: :thumbsup:

Elisa (later): canary results: p95 down ~18%, p99 unchanged, soft429 rate 0.6%, throughput -3%. kernel_change_rate fell ~45%. posting flamegraphs and nvprof soon.

Dan R: promising. next step: run longer 24h canary and check corp traffic patterns (seq_len distribution). if stable, roll to 25% then 100%.

Sara K: agree. remember to document config in runbook and include rollback probe for kv-cache regressions.

Elisa: noted, will update runbook + upload profiles. thanks all.
